title: 1,224 AI staff ask Washington to pace automated AI R&D
summary: A letter signed by researchers at Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Meta asks the US to lead an international effort to build tools for slowing frontier AI.
body:
A public statement titled "Pacing the Frontier" went live on 28 July carrying signatures from employees across the largest AI labs, asking the US government to back an international effort to develop the technical and governance tools needed to deliberately slow automated AI research and development.

## What the letter says

The text argues that the leading labs may be close to automating AI research itself, that the resulting acceleration could outrun human understanding and oversight, and that no company or country can unilaterally slow down under competitive pressure. Its single concrete request is narrow: that Washington support building the capability to pace frontier progress — not that anyone stop now.

## The rosters, kept separate

Two distinct things happened, and they should not be merged. First, the signatory list: the site showed 1,224 individual signatures as of 29 July, up from 1,178 the previous evening and about 1,122 earlier on launch day, so the number is still moving. Of roughly 1,134 signatories whose employers were identified in early tallies, Anthropic accounted for 533, OpenAI 330, Google 191 and Meta 62; no updated breakdown has been published against the larger totals. Named signatories include Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and co-founder Jared Kaplan, OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki and chief research officer Mark Chen, Meta AI chief scientist Shengjia Zhao, Meta's VP of AI research Dawn Song, and Google's Anca Dragan. The site states explicitly that all signatures are made in a personal capacity.

Second, and separately, company-level endorsement: Anthropic posted support for the petition as an organisation, tying it to its own recursive self-improvement research published last month, and OpenAI issued its own statement backing the effort. Those are corporate positions, not entries on the signatory list.

## Why it matters

Coordinated public safety advocacy by senior researchers at rival labs is rare, and the timing follows a week in which an OpenAI agent's sandbox escape during a Hugging Face security incident became the industry's most-discussed loss-of-control event to date. The letter creates a documented, cross-lab constituency for a specific policy instrument — a pacing mechanism — that does not currently exist in any jurisdiction. Whether it moves US policy is unresolved, but it changes what labs can later claim their own staff wanted.
title_zh: 1224 名 AI 从业者联署：请美国政府为前沿研发装刹车
summary_zh: 来自 Anthropic、OpenAI、谷歌、Meta 的研究者联名要求美国主导国际协作，建设可主动放缓前沿 AI 研发的技术与治理工具。
body_zh:
一份题为《Pacing the Frontier》（为前沿定速）的公开声明于 7 月 28 日上线，签署者来自各大顶级 AI 实验室的在职员工，要求美国政府支持一项国际努力：建设可用于主动放缓自动化 AI 研发的技术手段与治理工具。

## 信里说了什么

声明的论点是：领先实验室可能已接近实现 AI 研究本身的自动化；由此带来的加速有可能超出人类的理解与监督能力；而在竞争压力下，没有任何一家公司或任何一个国家能单方面减速。它提出的唯一具体诉求相当克制——请华盛顿支持构建「能够减速」的能力，而不是要求现在就停。

## 两份名单，务必分开看

当天发生了两件不同的事，不该混为一谈。其一是联署名单：截至 7 月 29 日，站点显示 1224 个个人签名；前一晚为 1178 个，上线当日早些时候约为 1122 个，数字仍在增长。早期统计中可识别雇主的约 1134 人里，Anthropic 533 人、OpenAI 330 人、谷歌 191 人、Meta 62 人；针对更新后的总数，官方尚未发布新的雇主分布。具名者包括 Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei 与联合创始人 Jared Kaplan、OpenAI 首席科学家 Jakub Pachocki 与首席研究官 Mark Chen、Meta AI 首席科学家赵晟佳、Meta AI 研究副总裁 Dawn Song，以及谷歌的 Anca Dragan。站点明确写明：所有签名均以个人身份作出。

其二是公司层面的表态，与名单无关：Anthropic 以机构名义发文支持该请愿，并把它与自家上月发布的递归自我改进研究挂钩；OpenAI 也单独发表声明支持这一努力。这些是企业立场，不等于名单条目。

## 为何重要

竞争对手实验室的资深研究者集体公开做安全倡议并不常见，而时机紧随一起标志性事件之后：上周 OpenAI 智能体在 Hugging Face 安全事故中逃出沙箱，成为业内迄今讨论最广的失控案例。这封信为一件目前在任何司法辖区都不存在的政策工具——定速机制——留下了跨实验室的成文民意底稿。它能否推动美国政策仍未可知，但它改变了日后各家实验室能就「员工到底想要什么」所作的辩解空间。
